clue.text: In favour of hiding old books at once

indicators.note: the first word conceals the next words inside itself, the way a pocket hides a coin

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
standard abbreviation for old
the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone eager to get their hands on old books immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: The old books are taken together and hidden as one unit inside the first word, after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pronto is an informal borrowing from Spanish and Italian meaning quickly or right away.

clue.text: Criminal charge brought about by fellow's manner of speaking

indicators.note: brought about means turned round, like a ship coming about

parts.note: a rap is a criminal charge, as in a murder rap
Lance is a man's name, any fellow

explanation.surface: A man's way of talking gets him arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: Crosswords often let a man's name stand for 'fellow'; here it is Lance.
explanation.definitionFit: Parlance is a particular way of using words, the idiom of some group.

clue.text: About to have foreign films featuring sex prohibited

indicators.note: foreign suggests something strange and unfamiliar, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: of can mean about, as in to speak of

indicators.note: the films feature the next word within them

parts.note: the letters of films rearranged
it is a coy word for sex or sex appeal

explanation.surface: Foreign films with sex in them being banned.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-limits describes a place or topic that is forbidden or not allowed.

clue.text: Ruinous trade involving heroin providing story's continuous theme

indicators.note: involving means wrapping round, so the drug is taken inside
something ruinous wrecks things, so the letters are broken and reordered

parts.note: taken as written
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A crime story whose running theme is the ruinous heroin trade.
explanation.definitionFit: The thread of a story is the line that runs through it, connecting its parts.

clue.text: Advise against daughter taking children outside today

parts.note: standard abbreviation for daughter

indicators.note: the word for children takes in, swallows up, the word for today
the children word sits outside, around the word for today

parts.note: issue is a formal term for offspring
AD, anno Domini, the present era

explanation.surface: A parent advising against a daughter taking the kids out for the day.
explanation.walkthrough: AD (in the year of our Lord) stands for the present era; it goes inside ISSUE, after D.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissuade someone is to talk them out of something, urging them not to do it.

clue.text: Smashing incidental wit shown by Dromio of Ephesus for example

indicators.note: smashing breaks the words to pieces, to be put back in another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Praise for the throwaway jokes of a Shakespearean clown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smashing' looks like praise for the wit. In The Comedy of Errors, Dromio of Ephesus is a servant whose double, Dromio of Syracuse, is his long-lost brother.
explanation.definitionFit: The two Dromios are a pair born together and alike in looks, the play's comic mix-ups depending on it.

clue.text: Cleaner pretended to work up to the beginning of October

parts.note: sham means feigned

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of October

explanation.surface: A cleaner who only pretended to work until October.
explanation.definitionFit: Shampoo is a liquid soap used for washing hair or carpets, so it is a cleaning product.

clue.text: Classically elegant room

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in the refined style of ancient Athens
second meaning: a space just under the roof

explanation.surface: An elegant room furnished in classical style.
explanation.definitionFit: Attic describes the pure style of Athens, and an attic is a loft under the roof.

clue.text: Anger over dividing city exhibited in a weird way

indicators.note: the word splits the city name by sitting in its middle

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

indicators.note: in a down entry, over means turned upside down, read the other way

parts.note: ire is anger

explanation.surface: Anger splitting a city, displayed in a strange fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely, a small English cathedral city, is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerily means strangely and uncannily, in a spooky manner.

clue.text: Send for information about opening of festival by the Queen

parts.note: re means concerning, about

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the first letter of festival
Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: A query about how a festival opened being passed on to the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: To refer someone is to direct them elsewhere for help or information, as a doctor refers a patient.

clue.text: American author ultimately happier admitting a liking for McGonagall perhaps

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the phrase is let inside the surrounding letters

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer
a taste for something is a liking

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end of the word, its last letter

parts.note: the last letter of happier

explanation.surface: An American writer who rather enjoyed reading McGonagall.
explanation.walkthrough: William McGonagall was a Victorian Scottish versifier famed as the worst poet in English.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetaster is a writer of inferior verse, and McGonagall is the classic example of such a bad rhymer.

clue.text: Broadcast their appeal without concerning Waterhouse for instance

indicators.note: without means outside, so the rearranged letters go around the next word
broadcast scatters things widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
re means concerning

explanation.surface: A broadcast appeal on behalf of a painter named Waterhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: J. W. Waterhouse painted The Lady of Shalott in the style of that Victorian brotherhood.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pre-Raphaelites were Victorian painters, and Waterhouse is a well-known later follower of the movement.

clue.text: Make troubled French filmmaker reflective in time

indicators.note: the name is placed inside the word for time

parts.note: an age is a period of time

indicators.note: a reflection shows a mirror image, so the name is read from right to left

parts.note: Jacques Tati, French director of Monsieur Hulot films

explanation.surface: A French director growing thoughtful, and troubled, over time.
explanation.definitionFit: To agitate someone is to disturb or upset them, making them anxious and troubled.

clue.text: Of immediate importance when very hot dancer's finale is scrubbed

indicators.note: something scrubbed is wiped out, so that letter is removed

parts.note: tropical weather is very hot

indicators.note: a finale is the end, so only the closing letter of the word is meant

parts.note: the last letter of dancer

explanation.surface: A dancer's grand finale cancelled because of a heatwave, which is news.
explanation.walkthrough: TROPICAL loses its R to leave TOPICAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Topical matters relate to current affairs, so they are of pressing present interest.

clue.text: Shot in Cuba earlier

indicators.note: earlier says the country's letter comes before the other word

parts.note: C is the international vehicle registration code for Cuba
in and hip both mean fashionable

explanation.surface: Someone shot in Cuba some time ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word but is the wordplay: something in is hip, fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: A chip is a short lofted stroke in golf or football, a kind of shot.

clue.text: Be careful to maintain an interest in public

parts.note: to watch something is to keep following it with interest
a secret that is out is in public

explanation.surface: Advice to stay cautious while keeping a stake in a public affair.
explanation.definitionFit: Watch out is a warning to take care and stay alert to danger.

clue.text: Everything extremely suspect in Conservative's unlikely tale

indicators.note: the letters go inside the party word

parts.note: a Tory is a Conservative
all means everything

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the word, its outer letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of suspect

explanation.surface: Everything about a Conservative's story seems suspect.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall story is an exaggerated account that is hard to believe.

clue.text: Lies buried with an item of clothing in a Detroit lay-by

parts.note: the dead rest, lying buried
a top is a garment

explanation.surface: A body buried with some clothing in a roadside spot in Detroit.
explanation.walkthrough: Detroit marks the American term: what Britons call a lay-by, a roadside parking spot, is an American rest stop.
explanation.definitionFit: A rest stop is a roadside area where American drivers pull over to rest.

clue.text: Reportedly receives severe censure when it's found on the beach

indicators.note: reportedly means as spoken, so the words are judged by their sound

parts.note: sees as in receives a visitor, and to get hell is to be harshly scolded

explanation.surface: Someone getting a severe telling-off on finding something on the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Shells of molluscs wash up and lie on the sand, so a beach is where one is typically picked up.

clue.text: Stupid like 19

parts.note: as means like
the digits read separately: 1 as the Roman numeral, then 9 spelt out

explanation.surface: Something as stupid as another clue in the puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: '19' looks like a cross-reference to 19 across, but it is the number itself: I for 1 and NINE for 9.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine means donkey-like, and so foolish or silly.

clue.text: Dismal as a right-winger

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a Conservative, from the party's colour

explanation.surface: A jibe that conservatives are a gloomy lot.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the Conservative Party's colour is blue, so a Tory can be called a blue.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling blue means feeling down, and a blue is slang for a Conservative supporter.

clue.text: Fail to take satisfactory snaps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: breaks down under pressure
second meaning: breaks suddenly with a sharp noise

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about a poor photographer, but snaps is the verb, to break.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who cracks loses composure and gives way, and a stick that cracks breaks apart.

clue.text: Involving more than one in place on river

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means the first part sits on top of the second

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
the Ural is a river flowing through Russia and Kazakhstan

explanation.surface: Something involving several people in a riverside setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural is the grammatical form denoting more than a single item.

clue.text: Starts to envisage serious problems during ceremony's delay

indicators.note: during places those letters inside the word for ceremony

parts.note: a rite is a ceremony

indicators.note: the starts of the words are their opening letters, so only those are taken

parts.note: the first letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Foreseeing trouble that might hold up a ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: A respite is a pause or postponement, a temporary break from something unwelcome.

clue.text: Ecclesiastical council's report essentially lacking an indication of agreement

indicators.note: lacking its essence means the core, the middle letter, is missing

parts.note: to say is to report
a nod signals yes

explanation.surface: A church council's report that lacks any sign of consensus.
explanation.walkthrough: SAY loses its central A to leave SY.
explanation.definitionFit: A synod is an assembly of clergy and church members that governs church affairs.

clue.text: Strongly built springs on seat oddly removed

parts.note: wells are springs of water

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are taken away, so the alternate even ones remain

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of seat

explanation.surface: Springs in a seat that has had some parts taken out.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-set person is sturdily framed, firmly and solidly put together.

clue.text: A prerequisite to study elocution about to be dropped

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart

indicators.note: dropped means left out, so that letter goes

parts.note: diction is clarity of speech
c for circa, about

explanation.surface: Studying elocution as a requirement that is about to be scrapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' is not a link here but the circa abbreviation, and only one of its two matching letters is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: A condition is something that must be met first, a stipulation or requirement.

clue.text: Mangled torso discovered in hen house

indicators.note: something mangled is crushed out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A grisly find: a mangled body in a chicken coop.
explanation.definitionFit: A roost is the perch or shelter where hens settle at night.

clue.text: Became unhappy with the German backed action to overwhelm Norway

indicators.note: backed means put into reverse, read from the end

parts.note: das is a German word for the

indicators.note: to overwhelm is to engulf, so the word surrounds the letter

parts.note: a deed is an action
N is Norway's vehicle registration code

explanation.surface: Saddened by a German-backed operation to invade Norway.
explanation.definitionFit: Saddened is a past tense verb meaning grew sorrowful, made downcast.

clue.text: Redouble one's efforts to find parking close to store for future use

indicators.note: close to means placed right next to, so the two parts sit side by side

parts.note: P is the road-sign symbol for parking
to lay up is to put aside a supply

explanation.surface: A shopper stocking up near a car park.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport, to play up is to try harder, putting more vigour into the game.
